title: .claude_current_state.json Structural Schema
description: Structural JSON Schema for .claude_current_state.json (ST-34, EPIC-06, v9.8, BLG-GOV-342). Validates the session-start state pointer's field types and presence of the core fields every engine reads/writes. This is a STRUCTURAL schema (field names/types/presence) -- it is distinct from claude/system/lifecycle_schema.json, which is the canonical STATE-MACHINE definition (valid `status` values, allowed transitions, guard rules). Both are referenced by .claude_current_state.json itself via the `lifecycle_schema`/`schema_version` fields (state-machine) and this file's own path convention (structural). additionalProperties is intentionally true: this file grows per-cycle with new ad hoc fields (e.g. `release_plan`, `active_pog`), and an exhaustive closed schema would need a version bump every cycle for no validation benefit -- the fields below are the stable, cross-cycle core every engine actually depends on.

active_cycle.description: The active cycle_id, e.g. '2026-09-28__release-v9.8'. Identifies the cycle folder under claude/cycles/.

status.description: Current lifecycle status. Valid values are defined in claude/system/lifecycle_schema.json's `states` object -- this schema does not duplicate that enum, to avoid the two files drifting out of sync on every new state added.

engine.description: Which governance engine last wrote this file (e.g. 'Sprint Execution', 'Release Planning').

last_updated_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the most recent write to this file by ANY engine. Added ST-34/BLG-GOV-342 -- roadmap_prompt.md STEP -1.6's state-age advisory reads this field and previously always fired (absent-field case) regardless of actual staleness. Every engine that writes this file MUST set this field to the current UTC time in the same write -- see shared_standards.md SS24.

last_sync_utc.description: Distinct from last_updated_utc: the last time an explicit `sync gh` (or similar external-sync) operation ran. Not a general write timestamp.

lifecycle_schema.description: Path to the canonical state-machine definition (claude/system/lifecycle_schema.json).

open_escalations.description: Map of ESC-* / ESC-EXEC-* / ESC-CLOSE-* IDs to escalation records. Each record's own shape is defined by shared_standards.md SS4, not repeated here.

deferred_escalations.description: Same record shape as open_escalations, for escalations formally deferred rather than resolved.
